ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a nitrogen molecule, N≡N, reacting with three hydrogen molecules labeled H-H on the left side of an arrow. On the right side, the diagram shows two ammonia molecules, each with one N atom bonded to three H atoms. Reasoning: Counting atoms on the reactant side gives 2 nitrogen atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms. Counting atoms on the product side also gives 2 nitrogen atoms and 6 hydrogen atoms. Since the same atoms are rearranged into new molecules rather than created or destroyed, the total mass before and after the reaction is the same.

raw_record.question_text: What conclusion about mass in chemical reactions is supported by the diagram of the reaction shown below?
raw_record.standard_answer: Mass is conserved in all chemical reactions.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: the left side shows N2 reacting with three H2 molecules, and the right side shows two NH3 molecules. Count atoms on both sides: reactants have 2 N atoms and 6 H atoms; products also have 2 N atoms and 6 H atoms. Since the same atoms are merely rearranged into new molecules, infer that the total mass before and after the reaction is the same. Therefore the supported conclusion is that mass is conserved in chemical reactions.
